notes.title: New free game: BACKPACKWARD
notes.notes:
We have a new sad story for you.

You’ve lost your stupid job at the Jack of All Fruits smoothie bar. Your friends and family have had it with your anger management issues. Your only hope is that your backpack appears to be a portal to medieval times. 

Play [url=https://ifcomp.org/ballot#entry-3192][b]BACKPACKWARD[/b][/url] for free as part of the 31st Annual IFComp. There's lots of great interactive fiction this year, and you can cast your vote if you play at least 5. 

See if you can make life rule again: [url=https://ifcomp.org/ballot#entry-3192]https://ifcomp.org/ballot#entry-3192[/url]

notes.title: In this austerely beautiful moonbase management game, "your only choices will be impossible ones"
notes.notes:
If you dream of playing a game set inside a diagram of a spacebase from an Usborne Cutaway book published in the 1990s, Kuu is probably for you. If you dream of being very sad on the Moon, tending sickly plants for 30 days by Earthlight, then Kuu is also, probably, for you. If you enjoyed Citizen Sleeper but wish it was as depressing as, say, Anoxia Station, Kuu is also also, probably, for you.

Read more

notes.title: KUU dev talk at NarraScope
notes.notes: [p][/p][p]This weekend Zach Dodson will be talking about books, narrative games, and the hybrid space in between, informed by the development of Kuu, Interactive Tragedy's next game. There are many great talks at [url="https://narrascope.org/schedule/#talk10"]Narrascope[/url] this coming weekend. Tune in! [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45527997/2f27a9efb602aa74bbf21eecf0666be85024ad33.png"][/img][/p][h3][b][url="https://narrascope.org/schedule/#talk10-g"]Hyperprint: From Novels to Games and Back Again[/url][/b][/h3][p][b][url="https://narrascope.org/speakers/#zdodson"]Zach Dodson[/url][/b][/p][p][i]Sunday 3:15 pm–3:45 pm (US Eastern)[/i][/p][p](Room: URBN-125) (remote presentation)[/p][p]How can digital storytelling change the printed book? [i]KUU[/i], my current work-in-progress, bridges the worlds of interactive narrative and hybrid book design, through a recursive creative process and a smuggling of technique: Twine and Ink for novel drafting and scanned print pages as a video game. I’ll explore the strange loop of developing an interactive game and a print novel simultaneously, focusing on how narrative structures, reader/player agency, and design constraints can be deployed across formats. Building on my illuminated novel [i]Bats of the Republic[/i] (Doubleday, 2015)—which featured diagrams, maps, easter eggs, and a sealed envelope containing Möbius loop of text—I’ve discovered that working to maximise the affordances of different media can create a narrative ecosystem that thrives. I’ll reveal drafting and development insights, including how the physical constraints of book design can inform digital interactivity, and how branching narrative design can inspire innovative print layouts.[/p][p][i]\[IF, game dev, publishing, cross platform][/i][/p]

notes.title: Sub-Verge, OUT NOW!
notes.notes:
Thanks for your interest in Kuu. An adjacent announcement: Our debut game, [b][url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/3487020/SubVerge/]Sub-Verge[/url][/b], has just dropped. It’s a cousin to Kuu, made by the same team. A smaller, submerged narrative puzzle, where you’ve got to talk your way out of a bubble-submarine. Before you get eaten. By an eldritch horror. From a poisoned sea.
 
We wanted to make a game where the story itself was key to the puzzle, and the more deeply you understand the characters, the further you can go. Once we sunk into the world of Sub-Verge, we discovered all sorts of strange life, and we hope that exploring the depth of character and world brings you as much pleasure as it did to us in creating them. 

The launch is part of the [b]LudoNarraCon[/b] festival, where there are other fantastic games on offer. We’re bundled with Herald, and a LudoNarraCon classic, [b]In Other Waters[/b], from the mind behind [b]Citizen Sleeper[/b]. 

Speaking of... today also marks the release of [b][i][url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/3659760/Subtle_Mind__A_SubVerge_prequel/]Subtle Mind[/url][/i][/b]; a prequel novella to Sub-Verge, exploring the events that led to the game’s deep-sea mystery. If you're into the world and want to go deeper, this is your vehicle. 

The Sub-Verge page is now hosting Raygan and Laura from the [b]Short Game Podcast[/b], our favorite podcast, for a special review stream of the game. But we want to know what you think, just as much. We are a small, sad studio. If you want to uplift our mood on launch day, review [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/3487020/SubVerge/]Sub-Verge[/url] on Steam, it makes a big difference for our small, sad studio.

We’ll return sometime with Kuu news, 
Until then, 
Interactive Tragedy, Limited.

notes.title: Annoucing our moonshot
notes.notes:
Ice-breakers are awkward. Hi. We’re [b]Interactive Tragedy, Limited[/b]. We’re a computer game company, but honestly, we’d really just like to talk about our feelings. And we’ve got a lot of them today, since we’re announcing... ourselves. 

We come from all over the world, but most of us are in Wellington, New Zealand now. We have special connections to Finland. We’ve worked on books and comics and tv shows together. And now, we’re making games...

[b]>Sub-Verge[/b] is the first! It’s an underwater puzzle you’ve got to talk your way out of—the story is the game, so you’ve got to really understand the characters and pit them against each other to achieve your ends. Which should be: escaping your claustrophobic submersible. There’s an underwater creature with a secret in its jelly-sac. It’s just bizarre enough that [url=https://store.steampowered.com/publisher/Pantaloon?snr=1_5_9_]Pantaloon[/url], an excellent newsletter-turned-publisher, in the UK has agreed to release it into an unsuspecting world, and we feel grateful about that. A big feeling.

[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images//45527129/58c3f1e8bb23f74d030ccad78a9bba25eacd2d37.gif[/img]

Other feelings have to do with [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/3442050/KUU/?snr=1_5_9_][b]Kuu[/b][/url], an atmospheric moonbase manager that we’ve been laboring at for some time, trying to get the ecosystem of game and story to live in harmony, hoping to avoid the schismogenesis that collapsed Biosphere 2, our beautiful failure of an inspiration. You can wishlist that game now, and if you’re at GDC, we’ll endeavor to get over any shyness and show you our work-in-progress.
[img]https://shared.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/store_item_assets/steam/apps/3442050/extras/KUU_1sleeper.gif?t=1741214405[/img]
We’re out of the hiding hole. As soon as our eyes adjust to the light, we promise more eye contact and more announcements and stories to come over the next few months. You can sign up for Sub-Verge updates from the Pantaloon newsletter, with an option to choose your allegiance, bestowing you with a[b] unique and exclusive Discord Role[/b]. For KUU updates, subscribe to the sporadic Interactive Tragedy newsletter at interactivetragedy.com

It’s really nice to meet you. I hope we can be friends. If you want to talk about your feelings, too: we’re listening.[u][/u]
